title: Flag overlapping in-flight tasks before parallel designs diverge
goal: PROBLEM: Two KainBain tasks can work the same code area at the same time with opposite load-bearing design decisions, and nothing flags the overlap until merge/review time, when the cost is a full rebase plus reconciliation. CASE STUDY: KainBain task 1cae113f-43ab-4613-801b-2de6297637fd (Surface runner git/commit and pre-commit hook failures clearly in the UI) built hook-failure surfacing that ran repo hooks on recovery commits and committed a test forbidding --no-verify anywhere in runner/, while concurrently merged task db49d6c6-bdd5-4600-aaea-15a71042ae20 fixed the same incident with the opposite decision (--no-verify recovery snapshots). The result was a merge FAIL with conflicts in runner/daemon.js and runner/project.js, a deep-review FAIL for semantic collision (any mechanical merge either broke the grep-guard test or reverted the merged fix), then a full rebase, design reconciliation, retargeted tests, rewritten ADR/runbook/plan notes, and re-verification of every suite. FIX (pick the smallest robust option): when a task is created or claimed, compare its touched files / problem area against other in-flight tasks and surface an overlap warning (shared files, same incident reference, or same subsystem) on the task and in the agent prompt; or add a lightweight relates-to / blocked-by link so the second task rebases onto the first before implementing; or require load-bearing decisions to be recorded in a shared ADR sketch before parallel implementation starts. ACCEPTANCE: (1) starting a task that touches files another in-flight task is changing produces a visible overlap warning naming the other task; (2) the warning appears before implementation, not at merge; (3) the linked case-study pair above would have been flagged.
